restoration_note: Teaching describes the four ordered receptacles into which the captured archonic host was distributed (firmaments above, eight earths below, encampments/strongholds around, and the star-sphere/zodiac), with the central image being the binding of the third-kind powers onto the turning Wheel — the cyclic process of purification by which Spirit and Living Fire receive ascending light from below and cast falling residue upon the natural mind. Most gaps are editor restorations of small letters/articles tightly constrained by Lycopolitan grammar (relative ⲉⲧ-, genitive ⲛ̄-, 3sg ϥ, ordinal ending ⲉ) or by repeating formulae (ⲡⲡⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ 'the Wheel,' ⲛⲟⲁⲙ 'powers,' the Father-of-Life/Mother-of-Life pair, ⲭⲣⲏⲙⲁ 'property'). Five gaps remained too damaged to restore: the 3-char verb particle at line 25 ({7}), the 4-char connector before ⲭⲣⲏⲙⲁ ({21}), the 6-char modifier after ⲭⲣⲏⲙⲁ ({22}), and the 13+2 char passage at line 56 ({23}/{24}) where the spiritual reading suggests 'wild beasts spread forth from his hunger' but the exact Coptic reconstruction cannot be made certain.

restorations.basis: Editor restoration of internal letters of ⲛ̄ⲥⲃⲧⲉⲩⲉ 'encampments/preparations' (from ⲥⲟⲃⲧⲉ); paired with ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲓⲟⲟⲣⲉ 'strongholds' as the third-kind ordered host of confined falsity surrounding the worlds — lexicon ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲙⲡⲟⲗⲏ/encampment.
Final ⲉ of Lycopolitan ordinal ⲩⲧⲟⲉ 'fourth' parallel to ϣⲁⲙⲧⲉ, ⲥⲛⲧⲉ, ⲱⲁⲣⲡ in immediate context.
Editor restoration of qualitative of ⲕⲁ 'lay/be set'; sphere of stars 'lies in great shame' — the sphere as cosmic circuit of natural states fixed in confined falsity.
Editor restoration ⲟⲩ[ⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲙ̄]ⲙⲛⲧⲁϣⲓⲡⲉ 'a great shame' with trace of ⲁ visible; the cosmic exposure of self-love under judicial restraint.

9-char feminine abstract noun ending in ⲉ, parallel to ⲙⲛⲧⲁϣⲓⲡⲉ; the teaching's central thematic word ⲁⲍⲓⲏⲧ 'concupiscence' recurs throughout (ⲛⲁⲍ ⲛⲟⲁⲙ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲍⲓⲏⲧ in line 26; ⲧⲟⲩⲙⲛⲧⲟⲩⲁⲍⲓⲏⲧ in line 35); the sphere is heavy in concupiscence-ness. ⲙ-ⲛ-ⲧ-ⲁ-ⲍ-ⲓ-ⲏ-ⲧ-ⲉ = 9 letters.
Middle of ⲡⲱⲛϩ̄ 'Life' — fixed by lexical context 'Father of Life.'
Standard Manichaean pair Father of Life / Mother of Life (lexicon ⲡⲓⲱⲧ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄ + ⲧⲙⲉⲩ ⲙ̄ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄); the Living Ones in the next line confirm the dual.
3-char verbal particle/auxiliary between ⲡⲉⲥⲓϣ 'her lash' and ⲁⲓ̈ⲧ ⲧⲟⲛⲱ; multiple equally plausible readings (ⲁϥⲣ̄, ⲡⲉ + verb, ⲣ̄ⲣⲱ, etc.) without distinguishing trace evidence.
Editor restoration of relative-attributive ⲉⲧⲟ linking ⲛ̄ⲟⲁⲗⲗⲁϣⲓⲡⲉ to ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧⲥ̄ 'in her' — the shamelessnesses that swarm in the sphere.
Editor restoration of ⲁⲩⲝⲁⲗⲝⲟⲩ 'they intermingled them' (Lyc. ⲝⲁⲗⲝ = ϫⲱⲗϫ̄); the fashioning-together of bound powers in the binding sequence (spread forth, intermingled, hung).
Editor restoration completing ⲡⲡⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ 'the Wheel' — recurring structural-term governing the entire teaching.
Editor restoration completing ⲛⲟⲁⲙ 'powers' — the standard Lycopolitan term for ⲛⲟⲙ/powers used throughout for the archonic host.
Editor restoration of postpositive enclitic ⲣⲱ 'also/too' — common Coptic discourse marker; fits 'those whom they hung also in (the) Wheel.'
Editor restoration; ⲍⲙ̄ ⲡⲡⲣⲟ-|ⲭⲟⲥ ⲉⲧⲕⲱⲧⲉ 'in the Wheel that turns' — word-break across line, completes ⲡⲡⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ continuing into next line.

Editor restoration completing ⲉⲧⲃⲉ 'because of'; ⲝⲉⲕⲁⲁⲥ ⲉⲧⲃⲉ ⲡⲡⲛⲁ ⲙⲛ ⲡⲥⲓⲧⲉ — 'so that, because of the Spirit and fire that turn there, they may abide' — fits the redemptive function of the Wheel as Spirit/Fire-channel.
Editor restoration; relative converter ⲉⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲡⲉ 'who are above' modifying the recipients of the conveyed light from below.
Editor restoration of genitive linker ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ before ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲝⲁⲓ̈ⲙ̄ⲗⲁⲍ 'love-of-strife.'
Editor restoration of definite article ⲡ- before ⲁϣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ 'multitude.'
Editor restoration ⲡⲭⲣⲏⲙⲁ; recurring lexical item in the king-comitatus catalogue (love-of-strife, kingship, likeness, desire of women, property, animals).
Editor restoration of genitive ⲛ̄ before ⲧⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ 'desire.'
Editor restoration of ⲛ̄ⲛ̄ⲥⲍⲓⲁⲙⲉ 'of women' (Lyc. ⲥⲍⲓⲁⲙⲉ = Sah. ⲥϩⲓⲙⲉ); the king's concupiscent desire as part of his exposed retinue.
4-char gap between ⲁⲍⲁⲛ (Lyc plural indef. article 'some') and ⲭⲣⲏⲙⲁ; could be a quantifier (ⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲛ̄ 'great'), connector, or modifier — no trace evidence to disambiguate.
6-char modifier ending in ⲉ between ⲭⲣⲏⲙⲁ and ⲙ̄ⲛ ⲛⲧⲃⲛⲁⲩⲉ; multiple plausible relative clauses or modifiers without distinguishing trace.
13-char gap; spiritual reading suggests 'wild beasts (ⲛ̄ⲑⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ) spread forth from his hunger,' but exact phrasing/word-order with adjacent {24} cannot be reliably reconstructed.
2-char gap with two illegible letter traces; insufficient evidence to fix together with {23}.
Editor restoration of relative converter ⲉ- of ⲉⲧⲙⲏⲣ 'who are bound' modifying the realms in the sphere — the central binding-image of the teaching.
Lyc ⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ 'entire' — final consonant lost; cf. ⲧⲏⲣϥ̄/ⲧⲏⲣϩ recurring throughout the comitatus passage.
Lyc ⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ 'entire' — final consonant lost; modifies ⲡⲥⲱⲱⲛⲧ̄ 'the entire creation' moved by the way-leaders.
